acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Guest Host Emanuele Berry talks to Nichole Hill about the Black movie characters Nichole was curious about as a child.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc:
A giant of the Harlem Renaissance, Paul Robeson was the most famous American of his day. Until he wasn’t. Nichole Hill tells the messy, complicated story of Paul and his wife, Essie Robeson.
This story comes from Nichole’s podcast, Our Ancestors Were Messy.
acts.credits: By Nichole Hill; Produced by Emmanuel Dzotsi
acts.title: The Was-It Couple

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
In 1865, a formerly enslaved man named Jourdan Anderson received a letter from his former enslaver, asking Jourdan to return to the plantation and work. Actor Laurence Fishburne reads Jourdan’s response.
This letter was performed in New York City at an event for Letters Live, which stages live readings of famous and remarkable letters in front of a live audience.
acts.title: Sincerely, Absolutely Not
